events.title: Chef first released
events.summary: Adam Jacob announced Chef on January 15, 2009 — a Ruby-based configuration management tool for converging servers to a desired state.
events.about: Chef describes infrastructure as cookbooks and recipes — install packages, template config files, restart services — with agents pulling from a central server. It competed with Puppet and later Ansible in the DevOps wave. Example: a `webserver` cookbook ensures nginx is installed, `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` is templated, and the service is running on every app node.

narrative.whyChosen: Chef brought idempotent, code-driven server configuration to production fleets.
narrative.whyImportant: It helped define infrastructure-as-code alongside Puppet and paved the way for Ansible and Terraform.
narrative.problemSolved: Manual server setup did not scale; teams needed repeatable, version-controlled system configuration.
